newsitem.title: USA: Retail trade group joins lawsuit against VISA.
newsitem.headline: Retail trade group joins lawsuit against VISA.

text.p: The National Retail Federation, a retailer trade group, said on Thursday that it is joining a pending antitrust action against VISA USA Inc and MasterCard International.
The trade group claims that the credit cards should not charge a "risk fee" to merchants on debit card transactions, since no credit or risk is extended in the deal.
Representatives from MasterCard and VISA were not immediately available for comment.
Merchants who accept VISA or MasterCard credit cards are required to accept the debit cards, which are tied to savings or checking accounts.
"These associations are charging a risk fee for what is a no-risk transaction....It's not the same as a credit transaction," said Pamela Rucker, a spokewoman for the National Retail Federation.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc and Limited Inc had filed the original suit against VISA, but other retailers have joined the lawsuit, which was later expanded to include MasterCard, Rucker said.
